title: Ontario police officer charged after woman pepper sprayed following arrest
summary: A 33-year-old woman was arrested shortly before 2 a.m. on April 29. According to police, Const. Brandon Mihalides used pepper spray following the arrest.
paragraphs: A London, Ont. police officer has been charged with assault after allegedly using pepper spray on a woman following her arrest earlier this year.
A 33-year-old woman was arrested shortly before 2 a.m. on April 29, London police said in a news release.
According to police, Const. Brandon Mihalides used pepper spray following the arrest.
In Ontario, the use of pepper spray is subject to mandatory use-of-force reporting requirements and a subsequent review process, police said.
During that process, concerns were raised about the use of force, and the matter was referred to the Major Crime Section to investigate possible criminal conduct.
As a result of the investigation, the 29-year-old officer is facing one count of assault with a weapon.
The officer has been reassigned to non-operational administrative duties, police said.

title: London Police officer charged with assault for pepper spray use during arrest
summary: A London police officer has been charged with assault and placed on administrative duties following a use-of-force investigation involving the officer's use of pepper spray during an arrest.
paragraphs: London·Breaking
A London police officer has been charged with assault and placed on administrative duties following a use-of-force investigation involving the officer's use of pepper spray during an arrest.
· Posted: Oct 02, 2026 8:46 AM EDT | Last Updated: 1 hour ago
London Police Const. Brandon Mihalides has been charged with one count of assault with a weapon and has been reassigned to non-operational administrative duties.(London Police Service)
A London police officer has been charged with assault and placed on administrative duties following a use-of-force investigation involving the use of pepper spray during an arrest.
Const. Brandon Mihalides, 29, of London has been charged with one count of assault with a weapon and reassigned to what police say are "non-operational administrative duties."
The charges stem from an incident at 2 a.m. on April 29 of this year when a 33-year-old woman was placed under arrest by London police officers.
Following her arrest, oleoresin capsicum spray, also known as pepper spray, was deployed.

title: London police officer faces assault-with-a-weapon charge
summary: According to the London Police Service, a 33-year-old woman was arrested by officers at about 2 a.m. on April 29. During the arrest, oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray was deployed.
paragraphs: A London police officer is facing charges in connection with an on-duty incident earlier this year.
According to the London Police Service, a 33-year-old woman was arrested by officers at about 2 a.m. on April 29. During the arrest, oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray was deployed.

Police said the use of OC spray in Ontario is subject to mandatory use-of-force reporting and review requirements. Concerns were identified during that review regarding the circumstances surrounding the use of the spray, prompting a criminal investigation by members of the Major Crime Section.
As a result of the investigation, Const. Brandon Mihalides, 29, of London, has been charged with one count of assault with a weapon. He has been reassigned to non-operational administrative duties.
“As this matter is now before the courts, no further information will be provided at this time,” London police said in a statement.
Mihalides is scheduled to appear in court on Dec. 30.

title: LPS officer facing charge in relation to on-duty incident
summary: London, ON (October 2, 2026) – A London Police Service (LPS) officer has been charged following an investigation by the LPS Major Crime Section into an incident that occurred during an arrest earlier this year.
paragraphs: LONDON, ON (October 2, 2026) – A London Police Service (LPS) officer has been charged following an investigation by the LPS Major Crime Section into an incident that occurred during an arrest earlier this year.
On April 29, 2026, shortly before 2 a.m., a 33-year-old woman was placed under arrest by LPS officers.
Following her arrest, Oleoresin Capsicum (OC) spray was deployed. The use of OC spray in Ontario is subject to mandatory use-of-force reporting requirements and a subsequent review process.

During that review, concerns were identified regarding the circumstances surrounding the use of force. As a result, the matter was referred to members of the LPS Major Crime Section to investigate possible criminal conduct arising from the use of the OC spray.
Following the investigation, Constable Brandon Mihalides, 29, of London, has been charged with one count of assault with a weapon and has been reassigned to non-operational administrative duties.

Policing depends on public trust and confidence. Maintaining that trust requires police services to have effective systems of oversight and accountability, and to ensure that when concerns regarding police conduct are identified, they are addressed appropriately, transparently and thoroughly.

Accountability is a fundamental principle of policing and public service. Our community rightly expects police officers to exercise their authorities professionally and lawfully. It also expects its police service to identify concerns when they arise, examine the evidence objectively and take appropriate action where warranted.
As this matter is now before the courts, no further information will be provided at this time.
